label: ML — Regression exercises (9 tasks)

lab.experiment_title: Implementation of Regression Algorithms Using Scikit-learn

manual_text:
Lab 06
Implementation of Regression Algorithms Using Scikit-learn

1. Aim
To implement simple and multiple linear regression with Scikit-learn and evaluate models properly.

Part A: generate and inspect the house data; look at correlations with the price; split 75% / 25% with a fixed random_state.
Part B (simple regression): compute the slope and intercept by hand, fit Linear Regression, confirm they agree.
Part C (multiple regression): fit all four features; reproduce the coefficients with the normal equation.
Part D (diagnostics): plot residuals against fitted values, a residual histogram and a Q-Q plot.
Part E (multicollinearity): add a nearly duplicate feature, compute VIFs.
Part F (real data): fit linear regression to the diabetes data.
Part G (regularization): compare plain linear regression, Ridge and Lasso.

13. Exercises / Tasks
Perform the following independently and include code, outputs and figures.
1. By hand: For the points (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 6), compute the slope, intercept, SSE and R² on paper. Check them with LinearRegression and r2_score.
2. Other single features: Fit a simple regression of price on each of the four features separately. Tabulate the test R² and RMSE and rank the features. Does the ranking agree with the standardized effects?
3. Split variation: Repeat the multiple regression for 30 different values of random_state in train_test_split. Report the mean and standard deviation of the test R² and RMSE, and draw a histogram. How often is the test R² above the training R²?
4. Learning curve: Train the multiple model on 20, 40, 80, 160 and 225 training houses and plot training and test RMSE against the training-set size. At what size does the test RMSE flatten?
5. Error metrics: Add one house with an absurd price (for example 200 million) to the test set. Recompute MAE, RMSE and R². Which metric reacts most, and why?
6. Interaction and curve: Add the features area² and area × bedrooms to the house model. Do the test RMSE or the adjusted R² improve? Explain, remembering how the data were generated.
7. Standardisation: Standardise the four house features and refit. Which quantities change (coefficients, intercept) and which stay the same (predictions, R²)? Then repeat with Ridge, where the choice matters.
8. Regularisation path: For the diabetes data, fit Lasso for 30 values of α between 0.01 and 10 on standardized features and plot every coefficient against α. In which order do the features drop to zero, and does the order agree with the CV results in Part F?
9. Heteroscedastic data: Generate data in which the noise standard deviation grows with x, fit a line, and show the funnel-shaped residual plot. Suggest two remedies (for example log-transforming y, or weighted least squares).
